Because Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention for this registration system, use the consular legalization-equivalent path: (1) notarization by a PRC notary public; (2) authentication by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial Foreign Affairs Office; (3) SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification or Taiwan-designated legalization office. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any direct or indirect shareholder, director, beneficial owner, institutional counterparty, agent, borrower, or platform partner, the compliance function must screen all identifiers against the US OFAC SDN and consolidated denial lists, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, PRC and Taiwan sanctions and wanted lists, and the FATF high-risk jurisdiction list. All foreign and domestic PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates will be subject to enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, negative news screening, and ongoing surveillance. Screening and adverse media checks must be refreshed quarterly, and any hit must be escalated to the designated AML officer before any incorporation step.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commerce Registration One-Stop Service and Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (onestop.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official legal name must be in Traditional Chinese and must include a company type suffix, a distinctive name, and a business scope descriptor; an English or romanized transliteration may be registered as an auxiliary name but cannot replace the Chinese legal name. The full name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any reserved or registered name in the same industry. Financial, banking, lending, P2P, trust, securities, insurance, and remittance tokens require prior approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission before name clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name pre-review is rejected, the applicant must first read the MOEA rejection disposition and correct or refute the stated grounds. Within 30 days of service, a formal administrative appeal must be filed with the MOEA under the Taiwan Administrative Appeal Act, and if the appeal is denied, administrative litigation may be filed in the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months. Before the six-month reservation expires, an application for a single six-month extension may be filed with the original certificate; if lapsed, a new pre-review application must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a high-risk special-license fintech operating as a P2P micro-lending platform, a bare virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable. Taiwan tax authorities, the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and banking counterparties require a physical registered office with a direct lease in the company name, active staffing, working equipment, server or cloud infrastructure, and operational records demonstrating local management and substance. A serviced office is acceptable only if it is a staffed, long-term commercial space with meeting rooms and a dedicated physical work area; a virtual mail-forwarding address or flexible desk mailbox will be rejected for tax registration, AML licensing, and bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk is high, approximately 70% likelihood of an unannounced inspection by municipal tax authorities, MOEA commercial officers, labor regulators, or FSC inspectors within the first 12 months. The inspection checklist includes lease and utility documents in the company name, social insurance and employee payroll records, board minutes and capital contribution vouchers, AML/CFT policies, UBO register access logs, loan underwriting and disbursement records, ACH or wallet payment integration agreements, information security and data residency controls, business continuity plan, and physical presence of responsible officers and personnel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for company name reservation via the MOEA online portal or in person. Provide the proposed Chinese and English names, business scope, and shareholder details. The name must not conflict with existing registered names. The application must be notarized if submitted by an agent. The MOEA will review and issue a name reservation certificate valid for six months. Ensure all information is accurate to avoid delays.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an appeal with the MOEA within 15 days, providing alternative names or justification for the original name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Joint Venture Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation and the Joint Venture Contract in both Chinese and English. All shareholders must review and sign these documents. The notary will verify identities, witness signatures, and affix the notarial seal. The notarized documents are mandatory for subsequent registration. Ensure the documents comply with the Company Act and the JV agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is declined, contact the notary office for clarification; correct any errors and resubmit for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application to the MOEA, including the notarized Articles, name reservation certificate, and other required documents. The application can be filed online or in person. The MOEA will review for compliance with the Company Act. Upon approval, the Company will receive a Certificate of Incorporation. Ensure all documents are properly executed and fees are paid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the MOEA's comments within 15 days; if rejected, file an appeal with the MOEA within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations (Tax, Business, and Financial Licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Local Business Registration Office, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, register for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the National Taxation Bureau, obtain a business registration certificate from the local government, and if engaging in financial services, apply for the relevant license from the FSC. Open corporate bank accounts and register for social insurance. Ensure all registrations are completed within the statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any registration is denied, follow up with the respective authority; correct deficiencies and resubmit within the prescribed period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan, ROC) through the jurisdictional National Taxation Bureau; online electronic tax portal: Tax E-Portal (https://tax.nat.gov.tw); e-invoice platform: Electronic Uniform Invoice Platform operated by the Ministry of Finance Fiscal Information Agency (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Taiwan JV limited company: (1) Obtain the required sectoral approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission for the P2P/micro-lending platform license or sandbox authorization before or concurrently with tax registration. (2) File name reservation and incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the Taiwan Company Act; secure the Company Registration Number. (3) Submit inward investment approval and remittance documentation, including Investment Commission approval if shareholder capital originates from mainland China or a foreign jurisdiction. (4) Within 15 days after MOEA registration or commencement of business, file the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Tax Registration application with the local National Taxation Bureau, attaching the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, responsible person identification, registered office address proof, regulator-issued financial license, and joint-venture ownership schedule. (5) Receive the eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBN), which serves as the statutory TIN and VAT/GST identity for all filings, electronic invoicing, customs declaration, and tax refund procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not maintain a check-the-box election for entity classification. Hybrid mismatch and controlled-foreign-corporation rules are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions; there are no elective tax classification mechanisms available to a domestic joint-venture limited company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Business Tax (Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act; VAT-type Business Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic threshold for an incorporated JV; tax registration is mandatory before business commencement. Small-scale merchants face thresholds of average monthly sales of TWD 80,000 for goods and TWD 40,000 for services, above which registration is compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates the statutory Uniform Invoice (GUI) system. Electronic Uniform Invoices (eGUI) are transmitted to the MOF Electronic Uniform Invoice Platform through Turnkey API or value-added network channels; e-commerce and platform businesses must issue cloud e-invoices with QR code and validation-code for consumer verification. There is no pre-issuance fiscal clearance or government stamping requirement, but invoice serial numbers are registered before use and the National Taxation Bureau reconciles issued invoices against filed Business Tax returns in bi-monthly assessment cycles.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under Business Tax Act Article 7. Goods physically exported from Taiwan to a foreign territory, and services supplied to foreign purchasers and beneficially consumed outside Taiwan, are charged at 0% instead of 5%. The exporter must be the person named in the export customs declaration; for digital P2P platform services, the contract, delivery evidence, and payment flow must demonstrate that the services are performed for and used outside Taiwan. Pure lending spread or exempt financial income is not eligible for zero-rating, but separately structured facilitation or technology service fees supplied to foreign borrowers/lenders may qualify. Zero-rated sales are declared in the periodic Business Tax return, and input tax related to those exports may be refunded through the export tax refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Declaration for exported goods) showing the JV as the exporter
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or electronic equivalent provided by the carrier
Commercial Invoice, packing list and underlying P2P platform loan-service agreement
Foreign exchange repatriation evidence: Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Proceeds Settlement Certificate issued by a Taiwan authorized bank
Digital service consumption documentation evidencing use or enjoyment outside Taiwan where zero-rating is claimed for cross-border platform services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau may review the export documentation bundle, customs outflows, foreign exchange receipts, and e-invoice data. If zero-rating is not substantiated, the export is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply, the VAT is assessed with default interest, any refunded input VAT is clawed back, and the taxpayer is exposed to penalties under Business Tax Act Articles 51 and 52 and the Tax Evasion and Penalty Act, including fines and criminal liability for forged or fraudulent export documentation. The statute of limitation for reassessment is generally seven years for under-reported or fraudulent tax positions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) [CBC]
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan maintains a managed-float foreign exchange regime administered by the CBC under the Statute for Regulation of Foreign Exchange. Current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, royalties and loan interest, are freely convertible and may be settled through any designated FX bank without prior CBC approval. Capital account transactions are generally liberalized but remain subject to statutory filing or approval when they involve foreign direct investment into Taiwan, outward investment, offshore loans or derivative transactions. Because this entity is a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture performing P2P micro-lending, the Financial Supervisory Commission treats the activity as a high-risk non-bank financial business requiring a special permit, regulatory sandbox authorization or licensed cooperation structure. Profit remittance to the PRC shareholder will be allowed only after annual audited financial statements, tax clearance, Investment Commission filing and CBC exchange-reporting have been completed. There is no requirement to surrender export foreign currency receipts into New Taiwan dollars; however, all cross-border receipts must be repatriated through a domestic authorized FX bank and reported. The CBC actively intervenes to smooth excessive NTD volatility, so treasury should maintain currency concentration limits, dynamic hedging and disciplined liquidity buffers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods and services exporters must collect the full invoice amount within the CBC-prescribed period, generally within four months from shipment date for goods, and must either sell the foreign exchange to a designated FX bank or credit it to the exporter's foreign currency deposit account at such a bank. The mandatory conversion ratio to New Taiwan dollars is 0%: no fixed portion must be converted, but the full foreign-exchange receipt must be repatriated, declared and settled through a CBC-authorised bank. Late repatriation, unapproved parking of proceeds offshore, or submission of inaccurate declarations can trigger a CBC audit, administrative penalties, suspension of FX dealer eligibility and loss of conversion privileges.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Eligibility and Legally Restricted. A Taiwan-incorporated P2P lending joint venture cannot use an unlicensed foreign EMI such as Revolut, Wise, Airwallex or other offshore digital payment platforms as its primary corporate treasury or settlement bank because the FSC and CBC require lending and payment activities to clear through domestically authorized financial institutions. Such EMIs may only serve as auxiliary collection or wallet-payout conduits if they hold a valid Taiwan electronic payment institution license or form a partnership with a licensed Taiwan bank that custodies NTD funds. Using an offshore EMI for client trust money would fail capital verification, expose the JV to illegal deposit-taking allegations, and create severe AML chain-density gaps. Viability is therefore limited to supplementary supplier-payment corridors after Taiwan bank accounts are established.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. At least one statutory director, the general manager, or a specifically designated senior officer with actual binding authority must appear in person at the Taiwan domestic branch for a due-diligence interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for high-risk P2P financial institutions. If the PRC-appointed director cannot travel, the JV may appoint a Taiwan resident director or manager through a power of attorney that is notarized in the PRC, legalized through the Taiwan Affairs mechanism or a Taiwan Overseas Mission, and accepted by the bank legal and compliance team after a live teleconference and certified copy verification. The Chinese shareholder resolution, JV approval certificate from the Investment Commission, company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, tax registration, and beneficial ownership declaration must all be produced in certified English or Chinese translation before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk licence dependence: P2P micro-lending is flagged as unlicensed deposit-taking or shadow banking if no Financial Supervisory Commission permit or regulatory sandbox authorization is evidenced at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSC business licence or sandbox approval, board-approved AML/CFT programme with transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, audited financial statements, business plan showing projected loan volumes, and a written undertaking not to solicit deposits or issue payment instruments without separate approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PRC shareholder opacity: a Sino-Foreign Joint Venture with a People's Republic of China ultimate beneficial owner triggers geopolitical, foreign-funding and financial-infrastructure scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment Commission of MOEA approval for the JV, notarized and legalized PRC corporate resolutions, UBO identifiers for every Chinese shareholder, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, PRC business registration and tax certificates, SAFE outward direct investment registration, and bank reference letters from the remitting PRC bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated retail disbursements and repayments create a commingled cash-flow profile similar to money-laundering or shell activity because of high volume and low ticket sizes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated customer trust accounts at a Taiwan designated bank, full digital loan ledger with timestamps, borrower and investor KYC files, automated transaction-monitoring rules, suspicious transaction reporting procedure, periodic independent AML audit certificate, and documented data-retention and e-discovery protocols.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from China via cross-border wires raises sanctions, evasion and purpose-code inconsistency risks if the remitter name differs from the approved contract counterparty or the narrative is incomplete.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original SWIFT MT103 advice showing the remitter as the approved Chinese JV shareholder, matching foreign-exchange purpose code for overseas direct investment, signed equity injection agreement, SAFE approval certificate, bank-internal clearing-line verification, annual capital verification by a Taiwan CPA, and a strict prohibition on cash couriers and virtual-asset intermediaries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions must first complete the PRC outbound direct investment registration with NDRC, MOFCOM and SAFE. The Chinese shareholder should remit through a PRC designated bank using SWIFT MT103 with remittance purpose code for overseas direct investment, naming the JV and contract number in the remittance narrative. On the Taiwan side, funds must be received into the JV foreign currency deposit account at a CBC-authorised FX bank. The receiving bank issues an inward remittance certificate showing the FX transaction category, and the JV then files the capital injection with the Investment Commission. The Taiwan bank converts USD, CNY or other received currency into NTD at prevailing spot rates after completing the CBC exchange declaration. Capital verification is performed by a Taiwan CPA who maps bank-in certificates, SWIFT advices and exchange contracts to the registered capital schedule; any mismatch in amount, remitter, purpose code or timing freezes capital verification until a rectification filing is approved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury flows are divided into three clearing rails. Domestic micro-loan disbursements clear through the Taiwan interbank NTD clearing system, ACH direct debit and local wallet payout rails operated by FSC-licensed electronic payment institutions with custodial bank accounts. Cross-border trade and service payments for software, cloud platforms, intra-group technology fees or data services use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers together with the CBC-assigned purpose code selected by the Taiwan bank. For future import-export operations, Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections are executed through the appointed Taiwan commercial banks. All outbound wires require dual-approval treasury governance, bank-issued digital certificates, a board-approved beneficiary whitelist, and a separate sanction-screening check at both the instructing bank and receiving bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts in USD/TWD and CNY/TWD are permitted only for genuine underlying exposures, with tenors generally capped at twelve months and executed through a CBC-authorised FX bank.

FX swaps in USD/TWD are allowed for rolling treasury liquidity management and capital-preservation purposes, provided the swap is documented with underlying trade, service or profit-repatriation cash flows and no speculative naked swaps are executed.

Non-deliverable forwards for TWD are not permitted as a standalone onshore Taiwan hedging instrument; NDFs may only be considered offshore and only for non-TWD currency pairs where the CBC imposes delivery restrictions such that only net settlement is possible.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps may be used solely to match long-term CNY-denominated shareholder loans to NTD cash flows after full regulatory approval and only with board-approved formal treasury policy documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting Resolutions and Financial Report Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by June 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers are liable for a fine up to TWD 200,000 (approx. USD 6,600); chronic failure may incur an order to wind up the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 to May 31 each year; extension to June 30 allowed when the return is certified by a CPA and filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A surcharge of 0.5% to 1% of the unpaid tax for every 15 days of delay (maximum 10%) plus annual interest; failure to file triggers a 10% penalty on the assessed tax and possible criminal evasion penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operations Report and Investment Approval Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed each year by May 31 after the close of the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 60,000 (approx. USD 1,980) per occurrence; habitual omissions can lead to suspension or revocation of the foreign investment approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Special License Review and AML/CFT Compliance Certificate (P2P Micro-Lending Platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application at least 30 days before the annual expiry of the special license; AML/CFT annual report within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expiry results in automatic withdrawal of the lending license and immediate suspension of operations; administrative fines up to TWD 5,000,000 (approx. USD 165,000) and criminal referral for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory CPA Audit Report and Annual Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements prepared within three months after year-end (March 31); filed with the registry within 15 days after shareholders' adoption, but in all events by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to TWD 100,000 (approx. USD 3,300) plus per-diem penalties; failure to obtain the mandatory CPA audit is treated as a material failure of corporate closure for the year.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Significant Controller Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Commercial Registration Office (Beneficial Ownership Subsystem)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronically submitted before March 31 of each year; resubmitted within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, new controller appointment, or change in ownership percentage above 10%
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from TWD 100,000 (approx. USD 3,300) to TWD 500,000 (approx. USD 16,500) under the Offshore Corporate and Beneficial Ownership Registration Rules; false declarations carry prison sanctions for responsible persons.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory certified CPA (independent auditor) report is required under Taiwan Companies Act Article 20 and the effective orders of the Ministry of Economic Affairs for: (1) any company with paid-in capital exceeding TWD 30 million (approx. USD 1 million); (2) any enterprise in the financial, lending, or insurance category, save for a company exempted by the Financial Supervisory Commission; and (3) any company whose annual turnover exceeds TWD 100 million (approx. USD 3.3 million) or whose total employee headcount is over 100. P2P automatic underwriting platforms fall into category (2) and are thus unconditionally subject to independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS (T-IFRS) for the consolidation, with mandatory application of IFRS 9 (financial instruments), IFRS 15 (revenue recognition) and the ASR/AML reserve computation standard applicable to non-bank micro-lending platforms; private SME standards may be accepted for unregulated affiliates, but the regulated lending entity must apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The JV must file an annual electronic confirmation of its significant controllers to MOEA by March 31 and also amend that record within 30 days of any shift in shareholding or controllers. A transfer of 10% or more in the equity of the Chinese/Taiwanese JV is subject to the prior approval (or post-filing ratification) of the MOEA Investment Commission and must be uploaded to the Beneficial Ownership Subsystem without delay. The annual confirmation must be signed by the JV manager and accompanied by an updated shareholding table.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,200 annually for a fully licensed corporate secretarial agent with a Taipei registered office address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 annually for a P2P platform-wide certified audit under IFRS 9 with internal control testing

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general free-zone tax holiday or patent-box regime is available for a P2P micro-lending fintech in Taiwan; the effective tax rate can be reduced only through eligible Research and Development credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, status as an emerging important strategic industry, or narrow incentive regimes such as the 3-year tax holiday for newly established qualifying science-park/key strategic businesses. The platform must nevertheless demonstrate real operating substance to retain any preferential treatment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ROC Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 100) and accompanying statement of related-party transactions and controlled transactions, filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance Tax e-Filing and Online Tax Application portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement; provisional estimated payment is due during July-August, followed by the annual return within five months after fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the provisional tax payment is due by 31 August and the final annual return is due by 31 May of the following year; a non-calendar-year taxpayer must file within five months after the end of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales and gross operating revenue, including platform facilitation fees, underwriting fees, loan matching service fees, and any recognized lending spread from the micro-lending platform.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrual-basis revenue must be declared on the Taiwan return when services are performed, economically driven, or applied in Taiwan; service fees earned from a non-resident related party must be arm's length and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, otherwise an adjustment will be made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct costs of providing lending services, including cloud infrastructure, data licensing, external credit scoring, collection costs, and charge-off expenses directly traceable to the lending portfolio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border data and cloud fees paid to a related non-resident party are deductible only if validated under Taiwan's Transfer Pricing Examination Rules; excessive management, technology, or data fees that do not reflect arm's length rates are non-deductible and may be recast as camouflaged dividends subject to 21% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or loss from lending and platform activities computed as Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The profit allocation to Taiwan must reflect the performance of underwriting, risk management, regulatory compliance, and user servicing functions; an artificial routing of residual profit to a non-resident algorithm owner without employees or investment in Taiwan will be adjusted by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, including personnel, office rent, marketing, compliance, legal, auditing, and other operating expenses incurred in carrying on the platform business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholder management fees and group service charges are deductible only when genuine services are actually provided and the non-resident service provider has real costs and substance; payments to shell headquarters or shareholders with no personnel are disallowed and are treated as non-deductible distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit or loss from the micro-lending platform, equal to Box 3 minus Box 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The operating profit must be consistent with the selected transfer pricing methodology and comparable data; if the operating margin falls outside the interquartile range, the authorities may apply a transaction net margin method adjustment and impose additional tax under Income Tax Act Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses, including interest earned on cash floats, foreign exchange gains or losses, disposal gains, penalties, and fines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid or credited to non-resident lenders, noteholders, or funding counterparties is Taiwan-source income when the payer is a Taiwan entity or the capital is used in Taiwan; a 20% final withholding tax applies unless a negotiated double taxation agreement or tax cooperation arrangement reduces the rate. Royalty and licensing income received by or payable from the Taiwan entity must be separately reported and is subject to source withholding at 20% on the non-resident recipient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before income tax, computed as Box 5 plus true Box 6 items less non-deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All recharacterizations by the tax authority, such as thin capitalisation, disguised equity investment, or treaty-shopping conduits, must be reflected before tax is computed; the board-approved financial statements and tax return must reconcile exactly to avoid a tax evasion finding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year net operating loss deduction, available for not more than 10 years where the enterprise has maintained complete books and records and the losses were assessed by the tax administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses claimed through artificial related-party funding arrangements, excessive intercompany interest, or sham loan defaults are not allowed; the deduction must be provable from Taiwanese records and may not be used to shift income to a non-resident parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after statutory deductions, and the gross 20% profit-seeking enterprise income tax before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The gross tax in this box is computed on the Taiwan entity's worldwide taxable income; dividends paid out of the after-tax retained earnings to a non-resident shareholder are separate and subject to final 21% dividend withholding tax at the time distribution is made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under Income Tax Act Article 108 triggers a penalty of 3% of the underpaid tax for every two months of delay, capped at 15%, plus statutory interest on the outstanding amount; underreporting and filing false data attract an additional tax of 2-3 times the evaded amount under Article 110; deliberate concealment through false fee records or fabricated related-party contracts is prosecuted as criminal tax evasion under Article 41, carrying personal imprisonment exposure; failure to withhold and remit non-resident WHT also subjects the platform to withholding penalties of up to three times the uncollected tax under Article 114.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% final withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, including a mainland Chinese shareholder of the Sino-Foreign JV, paid on the gross amount of the distribution before any deduction of underlying corporation tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty withholding, the non-resident shareholder must obtain and present a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the jurisdiction of residence, furnish a signed beneficial ownership declaration demonstrating direct economic ownership and risk exposure, provide board authority and substance evidence, and file the certificates with the Taiwanese payer before payment so the payer can apply the reduced rate or, if over-withholding has occurred, the non-resident must apply directly to the National Taxation Administration for a refund within the applicable time period. Relief is denied if the recipient is a conduit with no employees, premises, or business purpose other than the receipt of Taiwan-source income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates on payments to a non-resident without a permanent establishment are 20% for interest and 20% for royalties; under an applicable bilateral DTA or Cross-Strait tax cooperation arrangement the approved ceiling may be reduced to 10% for interest and royalties and to 5%-10% for dividends, subject to the limitation-of-benefits clause, exchange of information, and proof that the non-resident is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$20 million in aggregate annual related-party controlled transactions triggers mandatory Local File, Master File, and related-party transaction declaration preparation; country-by-country reporting is separately required for a multinational group with consolidated revenue above the NT$54 billion threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not have an OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but the tax administration applies substance-over-form and anti-avoidance rules requiring the P2P micro-lending platform to prove that core income-generating activities, including underwriting algorithm control, credit-risk decision making, AML/KYC monitoring, funds management, and strategic board decisions, are actually performed by personnel and systems located in Taiwan; failure to do so permits profit reallocation to the Taiwanese entity and penalty assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through underdeclared P2P loan facilitation income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors and tax officers divert a portion of algorithmic underwriting fees and platform service fees to an offshore shareholder wallet while filing a corporate return that reports only a fraction of true lending fee income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 110 imposes additional tax of not less than two and not more than three times the underpaid tax, plus interest; Income Tax Act Article 41 criminalises fraudulent tax evasion and carries prison exposure, fines, and confiscation of shifted profits on top of civil tax collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company Act Article 23 renders directors jointly and severally liable for damages caused to the company and third parties; courts may pierce the corporate veil by freezing personal bank accounts and ordering restitution of diverted fee income; travel bans are imposed on directors with delinquent taxes or penalties above the statutory threshold, and criminal conviction can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company and treaty-shopping abuse in royalty and dividend routing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The entity routes loan-origination software royalties and lending returns through an offshore paper company with no employees, no business premises, no board meetings, and no independent control, created solely to exploit a low-tax jurisdiction and avoid Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer Pricing Examination Rules and Income Tax Act Article 43-1 authorise recharacterisation of the transactions based on economic substance, with additional tax of up to three times the underpaid amount; submission of materially false transfer pricing documents attracts separate professional and corporate penalties under tax administration rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for disgorgement of profits shifted through the sham entity, the corporate veil may be disregarded where the shell was operated as an instrument of fraud, passports and exits are restricted, and criminal anti-tax-evasion charges may be pursued personally against the signers of the false transfer pricing statements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed banking, AML/KYC failure, and illegal micro-lending operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The platform conducts deposit-taking or public loan-funded micro-lending without the required special licence, while also systematically failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports on fraud rings using nominee borrowers to launder loan proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Banking Act Article 29 and Article 125 impose imprisonment of not less than three years and up to ten years, fines ranging from NT$50 million to NT$500 million, or a fine of twenty times unlawful gains; Money Laundering Control Act sanctions separately apply to failure to file STRs and to maintain effective AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, supervisors, and approving officers are personally liable for depositor and investor losses, assets may be protected for creditor restitution through veil piercing, the company may be ordered dissolved, and each director involved in approving the illegal lending operation faces criminal imprisonment terms of three to ten years plus disqualification from holding corporate office.
